review_type: PRIMARY original-mathematics gate objection, not independent second review
visible_symbol_reading: Q is a face identifier, as ordinary upright face annotations are in a wireframe diagram. It is the only known face identifier in the right drawing.
proper_rotation: A120degree rotation about the line through the octahedron center and the centroid of the Q face stabilizes that triangular face as a set. It cycles its three vertices and also cycles their three opposite vertices.
why_the_visible_outline_is_preserved: The regular octahedron vertex and edge sets are invariant under this rotation. Projection, camera and frozen visible/hidden geometry stay in place; only unseen face-number identities move. Q retains the same face set and centroid.
right_upper_rear_target: T,H,R, as confirmed by the question-mark anchor and original hidden edges.
printed_glyph_reading: If Q is treated as an oriented physical printed glyph and its direction is required to transfer, that can select the intended Q-apex-to-T pose and answer1. The source/frozen model adopts that pose. However the question does not explicitly distinguish an oriented ink glyph from an upright face label, and the renderer treats Q as a text annotation with a page offset. Thus the ordinary face-identifier reading remains a reasonable competing interpretation.
gate_scope: Hold unambiguous original uniqueness; do not change the formal answer, image, approved content, or frozen source interpretation. No style marks may silently add the missing orientation datum.
